newsitem.title: USA: Man arrested in Calif. shooting after McVeigh verdict.
newsitem.headline: Man arrested in Calif. shooting after McVeigh verdict.

text.p: Police said Thursday they arrested a homeless man for allegedly opening fire with a rifle on a power substation in California because he was upset over the Oklahoma City bombing verdict.
No one was injured in Tuesday's attack, but the bullets knocked out power to homes near the Emerald Lake substation, owned by PG&E Corp.'s Pacific Gas and Electric Co.
With the help of an FBI counter-terrorism squad, police said they arrested Peter Brooks Jaffe, 42, a transient from Redwood City, about 25 miles south of San Francisco.
After his arrest for the shooting, Jaffe told police of his "extreme dislike of the federal government," Redwood City police said in a statement.

Police and the FBI said they believe the shooting was prompted by Monday's conviction in Denver of Timothy McVeigh for setting off the truck bomb that destroyed the federal building in Oklahoma City in April 1995, killing 168 people.
Investigators found more than 55 rifle shell casings around the substation, a newspaper bearing the headline "McVeigh Guilty," and a Confederate flag on a nearby fence.
"It's clear that he had sympathy for McVeigh and that the verdict precipitated his actions," Redwood City Police Captain Ron Matuszak told Reuters.
He said Jaffe faces weapons, vandalism and possibly federal terrorism charges.

The shooting knocked out power to about 2,000 Pacific Gas and Electric customers. Two transformers at the substation were taken out of service because of the damage, estimated at $500,000, a company spokeswoman said.
